messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: RED ALERT: Elevated SRV lookup failures detected from services in us-west-2b (az-b). Error rate spike starting 14:02 UTC — ~12% SRV lookups returning timeouts or SERVFAIL. Pager sent to @sre_oncall and net oncall. See runbook: https://runbooks.internal/rdw/dns-cache-storm

sre_oncall: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Can someone post which services are noisy and whether this is localized to AZ-B?

eng_net: seeing heavy cache churn on coredns pods in azb. Cache eviction rates shot up ~30x. Also spikes in downstream latency to consul endpoints in same AZ. Possible feedback loop where failing SRV lookups cause aggressive retries.

alice_k: confirmed spike in k/v watch retries for consul leader in azb. consul metrics: `consul_watches_failed_total` increased. Might be saturating consul agents.

raj_p: digging into coredns logs now, tailing pod coredns-azb-3: 
```
Jun 12 14:02:12 coredns-azb-3 coredns[1]: plugin/forward: dial udp 10.2.3.4:53: i/o timeout
Jun 12 14:02:13 coredns-azb-3 coredns[1]: cache: eviction srv/_api._tcp.svc.cluster.local
Jun 12 14:02:15 coredns-azb-3 coredns[1]: plugin/cache: cache miss for _svc._tcp.svc.cluster.local
```

maria_t: consul raft logs show leader restarts on azb leader candidate nodes around same timeframe, likely due to pressure from watch handlers. This is consistent with a control-plane amplification.

support_lead: customers noticing 5xx from discovery-backed endpoints? Any known major customers impacted? I'll start drafting a status note.

eng_net: quick check — try pointing one coredns replica in azb to an azc resolver to see if cross-AZ forwarder bypasses the local degraded path. If consul agents in azb are overloaded, forwarding to another healthy AZ for SRV resolution should reduce load. Caveat: cross-AZ traffic.

sre_oncall: Agreed. Prefer config change over scaling out further (scaling might increase consul load). I will patch CoreDNS configmap to add a conditional forward for SRV queries to a healthy resolver. Applying with low-risk flag.

raj_p: patch ready, testing in staging then will roll to azb. Patch snippet: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns -p '\n{"data":{"Corefile":"cluster.local:53 {\n    forward . 10.3.1.10 10.3.1.11 {policy sequential}\n    cache 30\n}\n"}}' --type=merge
```

cloud_ops_bot: Running dry-run on patch -> success on staging (no DNS restart required).

alice_k: also throttling consul watch retries might help short-term — lowering retry backoff will reduce thundering. I'm preparing a temporary ACL on consul clients to slow watcher requeue.

support_lead: FYI internal ticket for impacted customers: CUST-2319, CUST-1982, CUST-2044. Putting them on priority incident email thread. ETA for mitigation?

sre_oncall: rolling patch to 2/3 coredns pods in azb now (one at a time). Will monitor metrics (cache eviction, lookup latency, consul watch failures).

incident-bot: Deploy started by sre_oncall on coredns-azb (job 98762). Estimated completion 14:12 UTC.

raj_p: first pod patched and healthy. Query latency for SRV down from 260ms -> 40ms for tests forwarded to azc resolver. consul watch failures decreasing slightly.

eng_net: good sign. I'm also adding a temporary iptables rule to limit UDP conntrack bursts from the coredns pods to consul agents to avoid swamping agents. Will revert after stabilization.

maria_t: consul leader in azb still flapping but leader election delays reducing. et al. suggests backlog clearing. Recommend keeping non-essential watchers paused for 15m.

support_lead: sent customer update: "We are mitigating a DNS/service discovery degradation affecting some services in US-WEST-2 AZ-B. Our engineers have applied a temporary forwarder to reduce load and are monitoring. Next update in 30 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sre_oncall: patch rolled to all azb coredns pods. Observability: SRV failure percent dropped from 12% -> 1.6% in last 10m. Consul watch error rate dropped ~70%. Still tracking KV watch backlog.

raj_p: logs now show successful forwards to azc resolvers: 
```
Jun 12 14:18:27 coredns-azb-1 coredns[1]: plugin/forward: sent query _api._tcp -> 10.3.1.10:53 OK
```

eng_net: marking cross-AZ forward as primary mitigation. Recommend we keep this config for the next 2 hours then gradually revert once consul KV watch backlog stabilizes.

incident-bot: escalation to on-call rotation next_oncall in 20 minutes. Handoff scheduled at 14:30 UTC.

sre_oncall: Handoff note for next_oncall: mitigation applied (cross-AZ forward), consuls showing reduced errors, leader election slower but stable. Actions outstanding: monitor KV backlog, review consul client retry settings, plan safe rollback path for forwarder. Link to runbook: https://runbooks.internal/rdw/dns-cache-storm.

support_lead: customer impact summary to send post-handoff: ~12% SRV failures impacting discovery-backed endpoints between 14:02-14:20 UTC, mitigated to <2% after forwarder. Affected customers notified.

maria_t: creating short-lived consul maintenance window to flush KV watch backlog and allow leader election to settle. Starting at 14:35 UTC for 10m.

raj_p: before we close: snapshot of key metrics: 
```
metric,since14:00
svc.srv.fail_pct,12
svc.srv.fail_pct_post_mitigation,1.6
coredns.cache.evictions.rate,30x
consul.watches.failed,70% drop
```

eng_net: noting follow-ups: - add circuit breaker to service discovery clients - tune coredns cache behavior for SRV records - add surge protection in consul agents - update runbook with cross-AZ forward as an approved mitigation after risk review.

sre_oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will leave monitoring on and perform handoff to next_oncall at 14:30 UTC. If anything regresses, page immediately. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Handoff: @sre_oncall -> @eng_net (next_oncall). Handoff message: mitigation in place, metrics stable but continue monitoring for 60m.

eng_net: acknowledged. I'll watch for regression and coordinate postmortem. Assigning post-incident owner: raj_p.

support_lead: prepping customer follow-up note and postmortem audience. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD.

maria_t: starting maintenance window now to drain backlog. Observability will update once KV watch queue is empty.

sre_oncall: leaving at 14:30 UTC — thanks team.

eng_net: taking over. Closing thread for active mitigation; keeping live log channel #incidents for follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident status -> MITIGATED (14:22 UTC). Contributors: sre_oncall, eng_net, raj_p, alice_k, maria_t, support_lead. Postmortem assigned to raj_p.
